world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Clark, David J. (1969) A grammatical study of Ekpeye, PhD thesis, SOAS; also Williamson (1988) Igboid chapter (cited on Glottolog ekpe1253); SOAS eprints unreachable

sources.citation: Clark, David John. 1969. A grammatical study of Ekpeye. PhD thesis, SOAS, University of London. 327 pp.
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: online with a university library login (also: harvard online access (harvardkey))
sources.note: Nothing. Ch. 2 'The Transcription' (thesis pp. 27-36) gives phoneme inventory, sec. 2.4 Tone (pp. 30-32): syllable is the tone-bearing unit; High, Low, Downstep + two falling glides; low lexical functional load of tone; downdrift. The words stress/accent (prosodic) do not occur anywhere in the thesis text layer.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger (ed.), based on mss. of David Clark and Kay Williamson. 2013. A dictionary of Ekpeye, an Igboid language of southern Nigeria. Circulation version. Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation. 43 pp.
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 2.3 Tone (p. iii-iv): 'Ekpeye has a typical Igboid tone-system with two level tones, and downstep as well as falling and rising glides.' No mention of stress/accent.

sources.citation: Ngulube, Isaac Eyi. 2011. Ekpeye orthography. In Orthographies of Nigerian Languages Manual IX (NERDC), c. pp. 48-66. (academia.edu 14521332, Wayback capture 2026-02-11; page text read from HTML)
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 5.0 'Tone system of Ekpeye': 'three contrastive level tones' (H unmarked, L, downstep) plus falling; 'vowels function as the nucleus of the syllable and therefore all carry tone'; tone has 'a very high functional load in Ekpeye grammar'. No mention of stress.
